museum.blurb: Commodore's office computer: 80 columns of green text, 32 KB, a proper business keyboard, and no colour, no sprites and no sound chip at all. Everything its home-computer siblings are famous for is deliberately missing.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 13 (trixie) kiosk runs VICE (xpet -model 8032) emulating a CBM 8032; streamhost captures the Linux framebuffer + AC97 audio exactly like every other tile. VICE bundles the Commodore ROMs, so this tile needs no external media — BASIC 4.0, KERNAL 4, the 80-column business editor and the character generator all come from the emulator's own data tree. The golden is the machine's own untouched power-on screen; the exhibit's interaction is the registry demoProgram, a BASIC 4.0 times table that fills all 80 columns. Drawn double-size (-CRTCdsize) on a 1600x1200 X root, the tightest advertised mode that contains the 1408x1064 SDL window. Keyboard-only exhibit; mono-terminal archetype — the 8032 is an all-in-one with an integrated 12-inch green monitor, which is what that archetype models. See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/cbm8032.md.

reset.fixture: Commodore CBM 8032 power-on screen (*** commodore basic 4.0 ***, 31743 bytes free, ready.) in VICE xpet, double-size on a 1600x1200 X root; golden INTERNAL snapshot restores the untouched cold boot. Nothing is curated and no post-restore keys are sent. Keyboard route certified 2026-08-09 AFTER the bake, against the restored fixture, in two framebuffer-asserted steps: the registry demoProgram's five lines typed at the tile's own 80/80 pacing take the green-pixel count from 1985 to 3861, and RUN then paints a 12x8 times table across all 80 columns at 7342. The readiness predicate is a BAND, not a floor — the PET's screen RAM is uninitialised at power-on and the CRTC paints it as a solid block of random glyphs (375726 green pixels), which an earlier floor-only predicate accepted as "ready". Keyboard-only exhibit (no mouse); AC97 audio, though the 8032 itself has no sound generator.
